ADMISSION CUTOFF ADVICE: IS THE GWA CUTOFF STRICT? (ADDITION TO THE ANNEX A CUTOFFS)
Source: strictness and lower-cutoff advice from campus information supplied by the maintainer (September 2026); cutoff values are from the LSPU Admission Guidelines, 1st Sem AY 2026-2027, Annex A above; exam and interview from the LSPU website admission pages. Cutoffs may change each year.
The GWA cutoff is strict. If your GWA is below the minimum for the program you want, you cannot be admitted to it; your only option is to choose another program with a lower cutoff.
Example: a GWA of 86 qualifies only for the GWA-85 programs.
Cutoffs for 1st Sem AY 2026-2027: GWA 85 for the three BS Information Technology majors, BS Criminology and BS Hospitality Management (5 programs); GWA 87 for BS Fisheries, BTLE and BTVTE (3); GWA 88 for BS Psychology, both BS Business Administration majors and BS Tourism Management (4); GWA 90 for Accountancy, Computer Science, Food Technology, Nutrition and Dietetics, Physical Education, all five BS Education majors and Elementary Education (11).
Meeting the cutoff is not enough by itself: applicants must still pass the entrance exam and interview.

presentation of proper credentials.

2.4. Admission Examinations. Student applicants should pass the following admission requirements administered by the Guidance Office:

2.4.1. Admission Test. It aims to measure the ability of the students.

2.4.2 University Qualifying Examination. It aims to measure the readiness and the competencies of students for the university.

2.4.3. Results shall satisfy the required standards of the chosen College.

2.4.4. An interview is also a part of the admission.

2.5. Percentile Rank. Students who meet the required percentile rank are eligible to enroll in their chosen field of study and are subjected to the College's screening policies.

2.6. College/Department Qualification. As a policy, students should have the following General Weighted Average (GWA) in their Form 138 for the following priority courses unless otherwise specified by the College:

2.6.1. eighty-five (85) and above for Accountancy, Engineering, Nursing, Information Technology, Psychology, Biology, Mathematics, Criminology, Agriculture, Teacher Education, and other Board Programs

2.6.2. eighty-two (82) and above – Hotel Restaurant Management, Tourism, and Industrial Technology
